text:
kai: Quick subtle DX report from the go sampleapp: cancelling a generator stream gives inconsistent errors and makes it hard to tell if resources cleaned up. Posting repro + ideas.

kai: Repro: start stream with ctx that has a deadline, rotate auth mid-stream, then let ctx deadline expire. Sometimes caller gets context.DeadlineExceeded, sometimes io.EOF, sometimes a SDK-wrapped 'stream closed' error. Hard to write reliable cleanup logic.

kai: minimal sketch:```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(parent, 250*time.Millisecond)
iter := client.Generator.Stream(ctx, req)
go func(){
  for t := range tokCh { iter.SetAuth(t) }
}()
for {
  _, err := iter.Recv()
  if err != nil { log.Println("recv err:", err); break }
}
// want deterministic: if ctx timed out, behave like context error and close all internals
```

meera: ugh yep. we've seen support tickets where apps retry on EOF and accidentally resubmit prompts. semantically EOF vs context.Canceled mean different things to callers.

jon: where is the inconsistency coming from? is the runtime sending a close frame vs the transport being torn down?

kai: looks like a mix: when auth rotate is mid-handshake the transport sometimes finishes and returns EOF; when cancel triggers force-close path we wrap and return context.Canceled. Also our current SDK wraps some lower-level errors into a generic StreamClosedError which loses original cause.

felix: recommendation: preserve cause chain and expose Err() on the stream handle that returns the canonical terminal error (context.Canceled / DeadlineExceeded / io.EOF / upstream error). That way onboarding code can switch on errors reliably.

meera: +1. And make cancel semantics explicit in docs: "If ctx is cancelled, stream.Err() will return context.Canceled (or DeadlineExceeded) and Done() will close when resources cleaned up." That reduces customer confusion.

jon: small API thought: StreamV2(ctx, req) returns (iter StreamHandle, meta map[string]string) ? we should avoid map nesting per agents.md but in code: StreamHandle should have Done() <-chan struct{}, Err() error, ForceClose() error.

kai: yeah my prototype: type StreamHandle interface { Recv() (Chunk, error); Done() <-chan struct{}; Err() error; ForceClose() error } The key is Err() to surface canonical cause.

felix: implementationally, ensure Err() returns context.Canceled when ctx.Done() closed first, even if transport later yields EOF. i.e. tie stream terminal error to cancellation origin. Use atomic compare-and-set terminalCause.

meera: docs: show idiom: select { case <-ctx.Done(): // cleanup; <-iter.Done() // wait for internals case err := iter.Err(): // inspect final cause } and show not to treat io.EOF as retryable if Err() points to context.DeadlineExceeded.

kai: will prototype Server-side inject test that delays auth handshake -> cause different closure types. will add example in examples/stream-errors that demonstrates Err() stable semantics.

docs-bot: friendly reminder: include a short blurb in onboarding "Stream error semantics" and add a changelog entry when you land this. Tag devex/docs.

jon: also add small unit test that cancels ctx and asserts iter.Err() == context.Canceled within 100ms to prevent regressions.

felix: +1. And add an integration test where UpdateAuth blocks; ensure ForceClose aborts UpdateAuth and Err() reflects forced close.

kai: perfect. i'll open draft PR "devex/stream-err-cause" with StreamV2 + compat shim and examples. will ping docs for onboarding blurb.

meera: thanks kai! this should make a bunch of customer issues much easier to diagnose. :thumbsup:
